newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FOCUS - Jardine pulls out of insurance JV.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Jardine pulls out of insurance JV.

text.p: Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd said on Friday it was pulling out of a life insurance joint venture after incurring losses and because the insurer's future strategy differed from Jardine's mainstream business interests.

But Anthony Nightingale, chairman of unit Jardine Pacific Holdings, said the buyout of its 50 percent share by partner Colonial Ltd would more than make up for losses made since the venture was formed in 1990.

Australian financial services group Colonial has agreed to buy out Jardine Pacific's 50 percent share in their Jardine CMG life insurance venture in Asia for US$163 million, the two companies said in a joint statement on Friday.

Jardine's listed Philippines' subsidiary, Jardine Davies Inc, would also sell its 40 percent interest in Jardine CMG's Life Insurance Company Inc to Colonial for US$15 million as part of the overall US$163 million transaction.
Jardine CMG has wholly owned operations in Hong Kong and Singapore and ventures with local partners in Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand.
Speaking at a news conference, Nightingale said future expansion strategies of the life insurance company differed from Jardine's mainstream interests.

"When we look at all the commitments that Jardine Pacific group has, such as our infrastructural investments in Hong Kong, other business we want to do here and outside, it seems to us that now is a good time to realise the value that has been built up in this life insurance business," he said.
"We believe it's a business that requires specialist skills to do well which comes better from our partner."
Nightingale also said the joint venture would require more investments in future which, when measured by Jardine's accounting methods, would not give good returns.
"Looking forward, because of the type of opportunities, there'll be requirements for more investments and by our method of accounting that's not going to show a good return," he said.

Nightingale declined to reveal Jardine's total losses in the venture but said the buyout of its 50 percent share was attractive and would enable the company to record a net exceptional profit of some US$130 million in 1997.

"It would be difficult to give a very precise figure on that (loss). What I'd rather say is that even if you take into account the losses, the price that was received represents a very good profit," he told reporters.

As for the life insurance company, which would have the right to retain its "Jardine" tag for the next three years, top officials said it was getting ready to bring its policies into China, India and Vietnam.
"Over the next few years, we're targetting China...we're also looking at investment in the medium to long-term in Vietnam and India," said Jardine CMG Life Ltd chairman Alan Beanland.
